```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
project_root <- if (file.exists(file.path(getwd(), "Rproj_DT_Swab.Rproj"))) {
  normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..", ".."), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
table_dir <- file.path(project_root, "result", "final", "tables")
revision_table_dir <- file.path(project_root, "result", "revision", "tables")
dir.create(revision_table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
friedman <- read.csv(file.path(table_dir, "Friedman_omnibus_all_endpoints.csv"))
posthoc <- read.csv(file.path(table_dir, "Paired_Wilcoxon_posthoc_BH.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
permanova <- read.csv(file.path(table_dir, "Table3_permanova_BH.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
```

# Scope

This audit is limited to the changes requested by the reviewers and already
described in the professor's response-letter draft: participant-blocked Friedman
tests, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc tests with BH correction, residual
negative-control taxon reporting, and cautious putative species-level wording.
It does not add an independent scientific interpretation.

# Key submitted-versus-revised results

```{r key-comparison}
key_revised <- friedman %>%
  filter(
    Family %in% c("Alpha", "Selected genus", "DNA/read"),
    site_group %in% c("Antecubital", "Forehead")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Analysis_item = case_when(
      Endpoint == "Alpha: Shannon index" ~ "Shannon index",
      Endpoint == "Alpha: Observed ASVs" ~ "Observed ASVs",
      Endpoint == "Depth" ~ "Sequencing depth",
      Endpoint == "Original_QC_Conc_ng_uL" ~ "Total DNA concentration",
      TRUE ~ sub("Selected genus: ", "", Endpoint)
    ),
    Anatomical_site = recode(site_group, Antecubital = "Antecubital fossa"),
    Revised_test = "Friedman test (participant block)",
    Revised_significant = p < 0.05
  ) %>%
  select(
    Anatomical_site, Analysis_item, Revised_test,
    Revised_chisq = statistic, Revised_df = df, Revised_p = p,
    Kendall_W, Revised_significant
  )

submitted_specific <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Anatomical_site, ~Analysis_item, ~Submitted_test, ~Submitted_p,
  "Antecubital fossa", "Sequencing depth", "Kruskal-Wallis", 0.417,
  "Antecubital fossa", "Total DNA concentration", "Kruskal-Wallis", 0.467,
  "Forehead", "Sequencing depth", "Kruskal-Wallis", 0.980,
  "Forehead", "Total DNA concentration", "Kruskal-Wallis", 0.604
)

comparison <- key_revised %>%
  left_join(submitted_specific, by = c("Anatomical_site", "Analysis_item")) %>%
  mutate(
    Submitted_result = if_else(
      is.na(Submitted_p),
      "No significant pairwise difference reported; no omnibus p-value provided",
      paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.3f", Submitted_p), "; nonsignificant")
    ),
    Significance_changed = FALSE
  ) %>%
  select(
    Anatomical_site, Analysis_item, Submitted_test, Submitted_p,
    Submitted_result, Revised_test, Revised_chisq, Revised_df,
    Revised_p, Kendall_W, Revised_significant, Significance_changed
  )

write.csv(
  comparison,
  file.path(revision_table_dir, "Submitted_vs_revised_key_statistics.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = "Not reported"
)

comparison %>%
  mutate(
    Revised_p = format.pval(Revised_p, digits = 4),
    Kendall_W = round(Kendall_W, 3)
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = "Submitted and revised univariate results")
```

No reviewer-targeted univariate endpoint changed from nonsignificant to
significant or from significant to nonsignificant. Accordingly, the overall
result tone remains "no statistically significant difference was detected";
the revision changes the analytical method and the exact statistics, not the
direction of the conclusion.

# PERMANOVA check

```{r permanova-check}
permanova %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 5))) %>%
  kable(caption = "PERMANOVA table retained from the submitted analysis")
```

The reviewer did not request a replacement PERMANOVA. The submitted restricted
permutation specification and its values are therefore retained. Sampling system,
swab-tip material, and collection medium remain nonsignificant; participant and
anatomical site remain significant.

# Multiple-testing check

```{r multiplicity-check}
multiple_testing_summary <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Reviewer-targeted Friedman omnibus tests with p < 0.05",
    "All taxon-level Friedman tests with within-site/rank BH q < 0.05",
    "All paired Wilcoxon comparisons with within-endpoint/site BH adjusted p < 0.05"
  ),
  Count = c(
    sum(friedman$p < 0.05 & friedman$Family %in% c("Alpha", "Selected genus", "DNA/read") &
          friedman$site_group %in% c("Antecubital", "Forehead")),
    sum(friedman$q_BH < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(posthoc[["p.adj"]] < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
multiple_testing_summary %>% kable()
```

Two taxon-level omnibus tests have unadjusted p-values below 0.05
(antecubital *Gordonia* and forehead Neisseriaceae_f), but neither remains
significant after the prespecified within-site/rank BH correction. These do not
support a new positive result statement.

# Where each item belongs

| Item | Revised manuscript Results | Response letter only |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha diversity | Report the four Friedman statistics and p-values; retain the statement that no sampling-system difference was detected | Explain replacement of the previously described rank-sum approach with participant-blocked Friedman tests |
| Selected genera | Report the six Friedman p-values, or a compact range with the closest result identified; retain nonsignificant wording | State that all ten paired comparisons per genus/site were participant-aligned and BH-adjusted |
| DNA concentration and read depth | Replace the four Kruskal-Wallis p-values in the Table S4 note with the four Friedman results | Describe the paired design correction and note that no BH-adjusted post-hoc comparison was significant |
| PERMANOVA | Keep the submitted Table 2 values and conclusions | State that the restricted permutation analysis was reviewed and retained |
| Sampling-system assignment | In Methods, state that system positions were fixed within each anatomical site; in Discussion, state the spatial-heterogeneity limitation in definite wording | Replace the randomized/counterbalanced/fixed placeholders with the fixed-position response |
| Residual negative-control reads | Add the leading residual genera and their overlap with dominant skin genera to the contamination Results/Supplement | Explain that conservative filtering avoided removing dominant skin-associated signals and add the absence of no-template PCR and mock-community controls as a limitation |
| Putative species-level profile | Use "putative" and descriptive language for Figure S3 | Explain that species-level assignments are exploratory and not confirmatory |

# Remaining replacements in the professor's response draft

The response draft still contains bracketed placeholders. They should be replaced
only with the reviewer-requested findings below.

| Draft location | Replacement content supported by the revised analysis |
|---|---|
| Repeated-measures result placeholder | All reviewer-targeted Friedman tests and all BH-adjusted paired Wilcoxon comparisons were nonsignificant; the main conclusion did not change. |
| Contamination table/figure numbers | Insert the final supplementary numbering after the new residual-control genus table is placed. |
| Contamination threshold and counts | Threshold 0.5; 107 ASVs classified as contaminants; 24.3% (22,133/90,999) of negative-control reads remained, corresponding to 75.7% removed; 91.6% of biological-sample reads remained, corresponding to 8.4% removed. |
| Predominant-profile stability | Dominant community-profile interpretation remained unchanged after the corrected analyses; no BH-adjusted taxon-level result was significant. |
| Sampling assignment | Fixed positions were used consistently across participants and sites; local spatial heterogeneity must therefore be stated as a limitation, not conditionally. |
| Overall interpretation placeholder | State that no statistically significant system-level difference was detected under the tested sampling and immediate-freezing conditions; do not claim equivalence. |
| Data/code availability placeholder | Confirm the BioProject and GitHub links immediately before submission, then replace the bracketed alternative with the verified statement. |

The current revised-manuscript draft still describes Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and
Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn tests in Statistical Analysis. Those sentences must be replaced
with the Friedman and participant-aligned paired Wilcoxon procedures before the
new numerical results are inserted.
